identificationModule.briefTitle: The Combination of Tacrolimus and Danazol as the Treatment of Steroid-resistant/Relapse Immune Thrombocytopenia
identificationModule.officialTitle: The Combination of Tacrolimus and Danazol as the Treatment of Steroid-resistant/Relapse Immune Thrombocytopenia: A Randomized, Controlled, Open-label Trial

descriptionModule.briefSummary: Randomized, open-label, multicenter study to compare the efficacy and safety of combination of tacrolimus and danazol versus danazol for the treatment of adults with steroid-resistant/relapse immune thrombocytopenia (ITP).
descriptionModule.detailedDescription: The investigators are undertaking a randomized controlled trial of 120 adults with steroid-resistant/relapse ITP in China. Patients were randomized to tacrolimus plus danazol and danazol monotherapy group. Platelet count, bleeding and other symptoms were evaluated before and after treatment. Adverse events are also recorded throughout the study.

armGroups.label: tacrolimus and Danazol
armGroups.description: Tacrolimus is given at a dose of 0.03mg/kg·d, and the dose is adjusted to maintain the trough concentration of tacrolimus at approximately 3-5 ng/mL for 12 weeks.

armGroups.label: Danazol
armGroups.description: Danazol is given at 200mg bid for 12 weeks.

primaryOutcomes.description: Sustained response was defines as the maintenance of platelet count ≥ 30 x 10\^9/L, and at least 2-fold increase of the baseline count, and the absence of bleeding, and no need for rescue medication at the 6-month follow-up.

secondaryOutcomes.description: Complete response was defines as the maintenance of platelet count ≥ 100 x 10\^9/L, and at least 2-fold increase of the baseline count, and the absence of bleeding, and no need for rescue medication.
Response was defines as the maintenance of platelet count ≥ 30 x 10\^9/L, and at least 2-fold increase of the baseline count, and the absence of bleeding, and no need for rescue medication.
Time to response was defined as the time from starting treatment to the time to achieve the response.
Duration of response was measured from the achievement of response to the loss of response.
Adverse events were scaled according to Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (CTCAE) version 5.0.
